title: The Second Glass
logline: Clara photographs Abu Haidar pouring tea at his Baghdad stall; he laughs at the result, bridging language barriers with shared joy.
synopsis:
Morning light washes over Mutanabbi Street as Clara Hughes returns to Abu Haidar’s tea stall, her vintage camera ready. The atmosphere is calm and warm, filled with the soft clinking of glassware.

Abu Haidar stands behind his wooden counter, preparing for another day of serving tea. He catches Clara’s eye and begins a practiced, graceful pour from his brass samovar into a small tulip glass, the steam curling in the sunlight.

Clara raises her camera to frame the moment, capturing the steam and the fluid motion of Abu Haidar’s hands. She clicks the shutter, freezing the image with a satisfying mechanical snap.

Lowering the camera, she turns it toward Abu Haidar to show him the result on the small digital screen. He leans in, squinting slightly, then bursts into warm, genuine laughter.

He gestures playfully at the photo, shaking his head with delight, while Clara smiles back, bridging the language gap through shared joy and the simple art of a perfect pour.

brief.text: The next morning Clara returns to Abu Haidar's tea stall on Mutanabbi Street to photograph him pouring tea behind his counter; he pours with a flourish, she takes the picture, then shows it to him on her camera and he laughs. One continuous scene of 5 to 6 shots, English dialogue for Clara only; Abu Haidar answers with gestures and laughter.

scenes.title: The Perfect Pour

beats.action: Warm morning sunlight hits the brass spout of the samovar. Abu Haidar, in his white dishdasha and red-and-white keffiyeh, lifts a small tulip glass. He tilts the samovar high, pouring tea in a steady, graceful arc into the glass. Steam curls elegantly in the shafts of light.

Clara stands just outside the counter, her vintage camera raised to her eye. She adjusts the focus wheel with careful fingers, framing Abu Haidar’s hands and the rising steam. The mechanical shutter clicks with a crisp, satisfying snap.

Abu Haidar sets the glass down gently on its saucer. He notices Clara lowering her camera and turns toward her with a curious, twinkling smile. Clara turns the camera around to show him the photograph on the back of the camera.

Abu Haidar leans in close, squinting slightly at the picture. His expression shifts from curiosity to delight and he bursts into a warm, raspy laugh, shaking his head and pointing playfully at it, without a word.

Clara laughs, covering her mouth slightly with one hand while holding the camera with the other. Abu Haidar claps his hands together once in appreciation, his laughter lines crinkling deeply around his eyes. They share a moment of silent connection.
